abstract: In this paper, a new topology of hybrid reluctance motor using a flux concentration technique is proposed. The relationship between the performances and electromagnetic geometry is investigated through an intrinsic parameter characterizing this novel structure. This study is applied to a 18 kW motor.

articleTitle: Harmonic analysis of a synchronous machine feeding a nonlinear load by a time-stepping finite element simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents a time-stepping finite element simulation of a synchronous machine feeding a fully controlled three-phase rectifier. The simulation provided the current and voltage waveforms which allowed the analysis of harmonics. In order to validate the numerical method the simulation results were compared to those obtained by tests.

articleTitle: A flexible gain error driven position controller for DC motor drives
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: The paper presents a novel nonlinear hyper plane error-vector driven bang-bang position controller for permanent magnet DC motor drives. The flexible gain adjusting feature of the combined position/speed regulation loop ensures robust position control and good tracking of complex position trajectory references. The control scheme is suitable for large robotic arm manipulators and guided vehicles.

articleTitle: Fault analysis and excitation requirements for switched reluctance generators
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Switched reluctance machines are a prime candidate for aerospace starter/generators and various automotive applications. The choice of SRM for a starter/generator application is driven largely by the perceived reliability and fault tolerance of the machine and its electronics. An analysis of the SR generator's faults and excitation requirements is essential to utilize the full fault tolerance capability of the machine in this application. Thus, research has been undertaken to identify, analyze and simulate the various fault modes of the SR generator. This research included an investigation of the generator's excitation requirements with and without faults. The investigation makes it possible to determine the size of the excitation source required during the initial build up of the generator's output voltage and under fault conditions. The SR machine, controller, EMI filter, excitation source and load were all modeled and integrated into a Matlab-Simulink model in order to analyze the SR generator system.

articleTitle: Sensorless adaptive neural network control of permanent magnet synchronous motors
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Rotor speed and position estimations in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) suffer from accuracy due to variations of machine parameters such as torque constant, stator resistance and inductance, especially at low speeds. Also, conventional linear estimators are not adaptive. In this paper, two neural network-based model reference adaptive systems (MRAS) for position and speed estimation are presented for PMSM drives. The first network estimates the rotor speed and adapts online to any change in stator resistance. The second network estimates the rotor position and adapts online for any changes in the torque constant. A q-axis model for stator inductance based on current is used. In both cases, the MRAS adjusts the neural weights to give optimal performance over a wide speed range. Simulation results showed the estimation adjusts well to changes in the motor operating points.

articleTitle: Tooth ripple losses in salient pole synchronous machines
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: In the present paper, the application of analytical and numerical methods to an electromagnetic problem requiring an accurate representation of saturation is examined. The problem considered is that of tooth-ripple losses in salient-pole synchronous machines. To calculate these losses, two methods, one devised by Oberretl and a modified version of the considerably older one-dimensional approach of Gibbs, are compared with the results obtained from the finite-element and finite-difference methods. Using a time-stepping finite-difference calculation, the influence of moving boundaries and the imposed DC field are taken into account for the first time in this tooth-ripple calculation. A saturation factor is defined that allows the designer to calculate the tooth-ripple losses of solid salient-pole synchronous machines for a wide range of machine size, taking magnetic saturation into account. To verify the theory, the results are compared with measurements on a small model. These measurements were done using a torque meter placed between the model and a DC drive motor and were cross-checked by the Poynting vector method. Rules and limits are given for the use of the analytical methods.

articleTitle: Problems in functional analysis of electric drive
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Nowadays, the designer uses an assembly of existing structures to design a complete static converter structure or electric drive. The resulting structures are generally very attached to a specific technology and are not very new. To avoid this, a functional description is proposed in order to take into account the technological aspect very later in the design process of the power part of electric drives. In such an approach, specifications are mainly defined by qualitative criteria. In the future, our final goal is to build an expert system for electric drive structure design.

articleTitle: Dynamic analysis of synchronous motor using vector diagrams
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Vector diagrams have been used for many years to help the understanding of the physical behavior of electric machines and to give a geometrical answer to a number of machine operating problems. Vector diagrams for a synchronous machine in steady operational conditions or even at the first instant of a transient state are the usual means of analyzing the machine performance. This paper shows the application of vector diagrams to represent the behavior of a synchronous motor during a transient process. As an example, the dynamic power diagram is introduced, showing the oscillation of the rotor following a sudden change in the motor operation. The purpose of the paper is also to point out the contribution of the intuitive mind to the solution of technical problems, a theme usually neglected in the educational system. It is the author's belief that the visualization obtained from geometric constructions is particularly useful for teaching purposes, since nowadays the widespread use of computers to solve numerically the machine equations, tends to move the student's attention from the actual physical phenomenon occurring during the performance of the electrical machines.

articleTitle: Analysis of PM tubular actuators
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: An increase in the force-density of tubular linear PM actuators can only be achieved by a proper dimensioning strategy. In particular, the magnetic paths and the magnets' dimensions can be optimised according to the mechanical load- and geometry-specifications.

articleTitle: A simple linear adaptive speed control of energy efficient DC drives
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This investigation is concerned with the model reference linear adaptive speed control of DC drives, incorporating separately excited DC motors, subjected to uncertainties including parameter variations, ensuring optimum efficiency. The adaptive controller, using the integral adaptive law, drives the plant output speed to the desired speed at any load and maximum efficiency is maintained by controlling the field current by an integral controller in the loss control loop (LCL). The stability of the speed control loop (SCL) has been established by using linear techniques (for the first time), ignoring the interaction between this and LCL whose stability is established using a new Lyapunov function. The simulation results confirm the analytical findings.

articleTitle: Single-phase DC drive system controlled by sinusoidal PWM full-bridge DC-DC converter with improved input current waveform
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents a single-phase DC motor drive system fed from full-bridge DC-DC power converter controlled by a sinusoidal pulse-width modulation and offers a high quality AC side current waveform. Two methods of control are presented such that the DC motor drive system may have bipolar or unipolar sinusoidally modulated voltage. Circuit simulation is carried out where the converter modes of operation and AC current harmonic spectra are presented.

articleTitle: An optimised variable structure control of a shunt active filter
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: In this paper the performances of a new shunt active filter control are presented. The proposed variable structure control strategy aims to reduce voltage distortion at the connection point of the nonlinear load and to cancel harmonic components from the system side. A switching optimisation circuit based on a digital switching table is added to the variable structure control. This control method permits a reduction of the switching frequency with an insignificant deterioration of the active filter performances. Simulation results on SABER program and experimental results show the effectiveness of the optimised variable structure control strategy.

articleTitle: Field evaluation of efficiency and prediction of steady state performance for induction motors based on equivalent circuit methods
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: The work proposes a method for field evaluation of efficiency and prediction of steady state performance for conventional as well as for converter fed induction motor drives, based on equivalent circuit methods. The motor parameters are measured by means of a standard PWM frequency converter and a universal analyzer with a Fourier analysis function, for direct reading of both total and fundamental RMS values of voltage, current and power. The results coincide well with the efficiency and steady state performance graphs obtained by direct measurements in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of a self-regulated, self-excited, brushless three-phase synchronous generator
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of a self-regulated, self-excited, brushless three-phase synchronous generator. The new generator does not require an exciter, and provides compensation for voltage variation without an AVR. An equivalent circuit, which can include the nonlinearity of the exciting impedance, is derived. Using the equivalent circuit, the generator's steady-state performance is theoretically predicted, and confirmed through experiment.

articleTitle: Effects of damper windings on negative-sequence components under line-to-line fault conditions
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper examines the effects of damper windings on negative-sequence components appearing in a synchronous generator's stator and rotor circuits, following an unbalanced disturbance to a one-machine infinite-bus system. The experiment has been conducted on a laboratory power system. The study generator is able to be operated both with damper and without damper. A line-to-line fault has been applied to the system. Both symmetrical component and Fourier analyses are used to investigate measured values of voltages and currents under the faulted conditions. Results will be helpful to understand rarely known behaviors surrounding damper windings.

articleTitle: Induction motor's contribution to short circuit current
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Simplified analytical models for calculation of the induction motor's momentary short circuit current are presented. Laboratory tests have been performed on two induction motors, in order to measure their contribution to short-circuit current. Results calculated according to the available literature have been compared to those acquired by testing.

articleTitle: Analysis of indirect temperature-rise tests of induction machines using time stepping finite element method
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: To be able to test the temperature-rise of induction motors with indirect loading is very useful for the motor industry. In this paper different indirect loading schemes including two-frequency method, phantom loading and inverter driven method, are surveyed. Their merits and demerits are pointed out. A universal method which can analyse all of these indirect temperature-rise methods is presented. The analysis is based on the time stepping finite element model of skewed rotor bar induction machines and the solution can directly include the effects of saturation, eddy-current and high-order harmonic fields.

articleTitle: Static characteristics of a new doubly salient permanent magnet motor
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: In this paper, magnetic field analysis of a new doubly salient permanent magnet (DSPM) motor is carried out based on the finite element method (FEM). Hence, the corresponding static characteristics, including PM flux-linkage, self-inductance and mutual-inductance, are deduced (the interaction between PM field and armature field are taken into account). A method for measuring the motor inductance is newly proposed. The theoretical analysis is verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Overview of electrochemical power sources for electric and hybrid/electric vehicles
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Electric and hybrid-electric vehicles are being developed and commercialized around the world at a rate never before seen. These efforts are driven by the prospect of vehicles with lower emissions and higher fuel efficiencies. The widespread adaptation of such vehicles promises a cleaner environment and a reduction in the rate of accumulation of greenhouse gases. Critical to the success of this technology is the use of electrochemical power sources such as batteries and fuel cells, which can convert chemical energy to electrical energy more efficiently and quietly than internal combustion engines. This overview concentrates on the work being conducted in the United States to develop advanced propulsion systems for the electric and hybrid vehicles. This work is spearheaded by the United States Advanced Battery Consortium (USABC) for electric vehicles and the Partnership for a New Generation of Vehicle (PNGV) for hybrid-electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Parameter measurement for synchronous reluctance motors considering stator and rotor iron loss
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents a parameter measurement approach for synchronous reluctance motors considering stator and rotor iron loss. The parameter measurement can be implemented by both constant-speed operation and standstill condition. In this proposed method, one can measure all machine parameters in the voltage equation for synchronous reluctance motors.

articleTitle: Robust control of field-oriented drive system with permanent-magnet synchronous servomotor
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: A simplified transfer function of PM synchronous servomotors is used to design various speed controllers: classic PI, H/sub 2/ and H/sub /spl infin// ones. The controllers are tuned for the nominal plant, around which the mathematical model of the machine was linearised. The vector control-based driving system was simulated, imposing different perturbations: load steps, moment of inertia, friction coefficient. Robustness was analysed.

articleTitle: Parallel capacitive and electronics excited stand-alone induction generator
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: A voltage regulated stand-alone induction generator system (IG), to work with variable speed and load, is proposed. The IG is simultaneously excited by a capacitor and an inverter. The control strategy is based on the instantaneous reactive theory. Experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Space phasor and FEM models of synchronous reluctance machine
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: A mathematical model of a synchronous reluctance machine based on the space phasor theory was developed. The third spatial harmonic of the magnetic flux density along the air gap of the machine due to the rotor magnetic saliency is considered. The distribution of the magnetic field in the machine is computed using an FEM model in 2D. The results obtained from both methods are compared and verified by measurements.

articleTitle: Vector control characteristics analysis in synchronous reluctance motor by using coupled FEM and Preisach modelling and experiments
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper deals with the vector control characteristics analysis in synchronous reluctance motor by using two approaches. The first one is a coupled finite element analysis and Preisach's modeling for synchronous reluctance motors, which is presented to analyse the characteristics under the effect of saturation and iron loss. In the second one, experimental results show the propriety of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Combined Simulink-finite elements approach to inverter driven induction motor
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling of a PWM induction motor drive by means of Matlab/Simulink package. The input parameters are calculated accurately by a harmonic finite element analysis. The coupled Simulink-finite elements approach is validated by simulating the unloaded starting.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic radiated emissions from electrical rotating machinery
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: The evaluation of the electromagnetic emissions from large power electrical rotating machinery is considered. The results of two measurement campaigns are reported: emissions are correlated with the operating conditions and the characteristics of the machine under test. The electric and magnetic field spectra are a reference for preliminary evaluation on similar machines; the results may contribute to assess suitable limits for electromagnetic emissions.

articleTitle: A novel spherical linear PM motor for direct driving infrared optical telescope
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of the drive system for SOFIA (Stratospheric Observatory for Infrared Astronomy). A special and unique direct drive motor design has been developed, which allows the telescope to be controlled in three dimensions simultaneously. The motor design and a first test arrangement are presented. Test results are discussed.

articleTitle: Laminated steel eddy current loss versus frequency computed using finite elements
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Eddy current loss in laminated steel cores is computed with unusual planar eddy finite elements over the wide frequency range produced in AC drives. The loss computed by the finite element method at low frequencies is shown to agree within 1% with a common simple formula. A formula used by radio frequency engineers is shown to agree within 1% with the finite element results at very high frequencies. At medium frequencies no simple formula exists, but the loss computed by finite elements is shown to agree reasonably well with some of the published data on steel laminations typically used in the cores of chokes and motors of AC drives.

articleTitle: Measurement of reactance of synchronous machines at standstill
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: When feasible, testing high power synchronous machines in a classical steady state regime requires a great deal of electrical power. This paper presents a method and its implementation for testing electrical machines in transient regimes, aiming at the reduction of the required power and minimization of the testing time. The direct-axis and quadrature-axis reactances are indirectly found by processing the acquired digitized samples of the step response of the stator current of a locked-rotor synchronous machine. Experimental results that have been obtained in a series of formal tests, illustrates the large applicability of this method.

articleTitle: Design and optimization, steady-state and dynamic analysis of synchronous reluctance motors controlled by voltage-fed converters with nonlinear controllers
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents innovative results to improve the design and manufacture of high-performance synchronous reluctance machines. These results have been obtained from our research in analyzing and synthesizing advanced control algorithms to promote the competitiveness of three-phase synchronous reluctance machines in electric drives in comparison with permanent-magnet synchronous motors and induction machines. These results have direct application in the design and manufacture of electric- and hybrid-electric drivetrains for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles. First, we report on the dynamic optimization of medium duty synchronous reluctance machines described by nonlinear differential equations. Second, we describe a new design optimization method, based upon nonlinear electromagnetic analysis, to improve steady-state performance and to enhance the operating envelope. Highly efficient, high-speed synchronous reluctance motors, ranging from 10 kW to 100 kW, were manufactured and tested. The design methods ensure cost-effective production of a new generation of state-of-the-art synchronous reluctance motors. This paper develops a nonlinear model of synchronous reluctance motors that incorporates saturation effects. Kirchhoff's and Newton's laws are used to derive the models. The application of Park's transformation results in a set of differential equations in the rotor reference frame; the q-, d- and zero-axis voltage and current quantities are used in analysis, modeling and design. Robust controllers are developed to guarantee closed-loop system stability and attain the disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: Effect of pole to slot number ratio on back-EMF constant of BLDC motor with nonoverlapping stator winding
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents a general expression of back-EMF constant of 3-phase permanent magnet brushless DC (BLDC) motor with nonoverlapping stator winding. From the expression, any possible combinations of pole and slot numbers are found and the value of back-EMF constant is compared in the several cases of different pole to slot number ratios and airgap flux density waveforms.

articleTitle: 80C196MC microcontroller-based inverter motor control and IR2130 six-output IGBT driver
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper describes how to apply the IR2130 to an inverter motor control and presents an overview of an 8xC196MC controller-based IGBT inverter motor control design. The IR2130 six-channel gate drivers perform all the requirements for interfacing logic level control circuits to high power IGBT devices.

articleTitle: Synchronous machine outages resulting from winding failures and defects
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: The paper reviews the synchronous machine forced outages experienced by one electric utility over a 30 year period which resulted from winding failure and other defects. The causes of failure include water, other contaminants, insufficient cooling, inadequate protective relaying or monitoring, bad joints, loose laminations, loose windings, component fatigue, inappropriate insulating materials, manufacturing problems, damage during installation and human error. This provides an indication where monitoring, testing and maintenance activities should be directed.

articleTitle: Mechanical behavior of hydrogenerator endwindings
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper presents experimental investigations on hydrogenerator endwinding vibrations and temperatures. In steady-state operation, links between machine load, winding mechanical characteristics, and temperature are discussed. Viscoelastic properties of coil composite sections are proved. Under transient operation (starting, stop) time frequency analysis is applied to detect machine natural frequencies.

articleTitle: Combined time-harmonic-transient approach to calculate the steady-state behaviour of induction machines
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: Due to less computational expenses, a time-harmonic approach is often preferred over a transient approach to calculate the steady-state behaviour of induction machines. However the computation time of the transient approach with a one-step time-stepping scheme is significantly reduced by using a combined time-harmonic transient approach and by varying the parameter which determines the difference scheme with time.

articleTitle: A methodology for using morsels continuous linear functions in gradient optimisation of electrical devices
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: This paper explains how to integrate morsels continuous linear functions to analytical models, calculating the gradient as strictly as possible, in order to perform optimisation. The example of inductance in terms of rotor position in the switched reluctance motor (SRM) is given.

articleTitle: The development of a skid-prevented direct drive system for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: A mathematical model for a switched reluctance motor (SRM) is developed. Then a fuzzy rule base is constructed and drive system's simulation is achieved. Simulation results show that the system has a good anti-skidding property and torque-balancing ability. A laboratory model is formed and experimental results are recorded, which are in good agreement with those of simulation.

articleTitle: Variable-frequency starting of squirrel cage induction motors
publicationTitle: IEEE International Electric Machines and Drives Conference. IEMDC'99. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX272)
abstract: The present paper describes an improved method of starting induction motors using variable frequency and voltage in which series connected capacitors and saturable reactors are connected across each phase of an auxiliary stator winding.
